These are fairly standard credit features like grade, sub_grade, dti, and int_rate, likely assigned at underwriting time so they shouldn't be circular or leaky. I'm now considering what else could make the temporally-split evaluation (2014-2016 train, 2017 test) misleading despite the split, starting with possible data leakage from features that reflect post-origination information.

The classic Lending Club leakage issue comes to mind: fields like out_prncp, total_rec_prncp, last_pymnt_amnt, recoveries, and collection_recovery_fee are only known after the loan's outcome, so including them would leak future information into a model meant to predict risk at application time. I should search through the top 180 features for anything with these suspicious names.
